items.statement: Debora fell in the kitchen on 2026-10-02 while reaching for a cabinet. She had a small left forearm skin tear and denied head strike or loss of consciousness. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 2026-10-02 nursing note.

items.statement: On 2026-10-05 PT found her gait slow and unsteady with intermittent cane use, and Timed Up and Go was 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly.

items.statement: OT on 2026-10-26 found she now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, and she was independent at the last review. items.verifier_note: The OT and home care aide notes match every detail, including the change from independent at last review.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He requested respite, and respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches all details.

items.verifier_note: Sertraline start date, PHQ-9, 4-week recheck and pharmacist reconciliation are all in the sources. The medication record shows no stop. items.statement: Debora is avoiding showers out of fear of slipping (2026-10-19), and depressive symptoms were treated starting 2026-09-13.
items.verifier_note: The shower avoidance on 10-19 and the sertraline start on 09-13 are supported. The statement says depressive symptoms were 'treated', which overstates a medication start. The notes give no evidence of treatment outcome.

What respite and evening support can be arranged for Kevin, and when will it start?
Was the 4-week sertraline recheck done? Should the fall be reviewed alongside the new medication, and should mood be reassessed?
Should the team arrange the flu vaccine for this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and the prior IDT review date so every check covers only the period since last review.

Falls and injuries: count falls, near-falls, and fall-related injuries in the window; check whether any fall occurred while on new or changed medications (sertraline started 2026-09-13 can cause dizziness, hyponatremia, or bleeding risk with clopidogrel).
ED visits and hospital admissions in the window, including reasons and discharge summaries; flag any chest pain, cardiac, or COPD-exacerbation presentations given ischemic heart disease and COPD.

Medication reconciliation: confirm sertraline 25 mg start on 2026-09-13 and its indication (PHQ-9 of 14), check for follow-up sodium level and bleeding symptoms, and confirm the prescriber and monitoring plan.

Antithrombotic and cardiac meds: verify clopidogrel 75 mg, simvastatin 20 mg, and metoprolol succinate 100 mg are being taken as prescribed with no recent holds, stops, or refill gaps; check nitroglycerin spray supply and expiry.

Respiratory meds: review fluticasone/salmeterol and albuterol use frequency, rescue inhaler use trend, oxygen use if any, and technique or adherence issues with the dry powder inhaler; note any new steroid courses or antibiotics.
Blood pressure, heart rate, and weight trend across the window, given metoprolol, obesity (BMI 30+), and ischemic heart disease; flag weight change of more than 5% or new edema.
Thyroid: confirm levothyroxine 0.075 mg adherence and check whether a TSH result is due or was drawn in the window.

Mood, cognition, and function: repeat PHQ-9 status and suicidality screen after the sertraline start, review sleep and appetite, a brief cognitive screen if noted, and ADL/IADL changes including mobility and self-management of chronic pain.

Chronic pain and preventive/oncology follow-up: review pain scores and analgesic use (none listed as active, so check for OTC or PRN use), breast cancer surveillance status and oncology follow-up, glycemic monitoring given prediabetes, and caregiver situation, social supports, and attendance at the IDT and care-plan items coming due before the next review.
